---
title: "Development"
---

Build phit from a checkout, run its tests, and change the implementation. To use
phit in an application, see [Installation](installation.qmd). Run the commands
from the repository root.

## Environment

The setup follows the official [ext-php-rs installation guide](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/installation.html)
and [Hello World build workflow](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/hello_world.html):

```sh
# macOS: Xcode command-line tools, Rust, PHP (includes headers), libclang
xcode-select --install
brew install rust php llvm
export PHP="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php-config"
export PATH="$(brew --prefix php)/bin:$PATH"
# If bindgen cannot find libclang:
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
```

Linux (Debian or Ubuntu with PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 in the configured repositories):

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential clang libclang-dev php-cli php-dev curl
# Install stable Rust using https://rustup.rs, then source ~/.cargo/env.
export PHP="$(command -v php)"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(command -v php-config)"
```

- Check `php -v`, `php-config --version`, and `rustc --version`.
- `php` and `php-config` must come from the same installation, with the same
  architecture, thread safety, and debug mode.
- `scripts/check` and `scripts/check-fpm` take PHP from `php-config
  --php-binary` unless `PHP` is set, so another `php` earlier on PATH, such as
  Herd's, does not affect them. Commands you run by hand still need the matching
  `php`.
- On macOS, the linker configuration lets PHP resolve symbols when it loads the
  extension. Linux needs no extra linker flags.

With Homebrew LLVM's libclang on macOS, also select the matching compiler and
header directory. Xcode's older `arm_neon.h` with a newer libclang fails to
build:

```sh
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
export CC="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang"
export CXX="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang++"
export BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS="-resource-dir=$($CC -print-resource-dir) -isysroot=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)"
```

## Build and run

```sh
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
# macOS; on Linux the file is libphit.so.
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/ols.php
```

- Each suite in `tests/` and each script in `examples/` runs the same way.
  `./scripts/check` runs all of them.
- `-n` skips the ini files, so the tests run against this build only.
- To load the build permanently, run `cargo build -p phit --release --locked`
  and add `extension=/absolute/path/to/target/release/libphit.dylib` (Linux:
  `.so`) to the php.ini that `php --ini` shows. The optional
  [cargo-php workflow](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/cargo-php.html)
  (`cargo install cargo-php --locked`, then `cargo php install --release` from
  `crates/php-extension`) edits php.ini for you, so back it up first.
- Rebuild for each PHP version.

[Installation](installation.qmd) covers PIE and the prebuilt binaries.
[Deploying to servers](deployment.qmd) covers containers and PHP-FPM, and
[Releasing](releasing.qmd) covers release artifacts.

## Numerical dependency policy

- Linear algebra uses nalgebra's Rust-native SVD, QR, Cholesky, triangular
  solves, and pivoted LU. There is one numerical path, with no BLAS or LAPACK
  dependency and no backend selection.
- The general mixed fitter uses the pinned Rust-native `bobyqa` and `argmin`
  (Nelder–Mead) crates, which add no C, Fortran, BLAS, or LAPACK requirement.
- An external numerical backend needs a concrete requirement that justifies the
  extra build and deployment work. An earlier Apple Accelerate trial was removed;
  its results are kept as
  [historical benchmark evidence](benchmarks/ols.qmd#apple-accelerate-experiment).

## Changing the implementation

- Keep statistical calculations in `crates/stats-core` and PHP conversion in
  `crates/php-extension`.
- Use established numerical crates, and check their APIs against the versions
  in `Cargo.lock`.
- Explain important mathematical steps next to the code.
- Update the contracts and reference tests when behavior changes.
- Do not add abstractions for hypothetical models.

`./scripts/check` runs the offline checks: Rust tests and clippy, every PHP
suite and example, the stub and signature checks, the reference manifest, and
the site export. Run it before pushing. [Verification](verification.qmd) lists
the further checks for each kind of change, and
[R compatibility](r-compatibility.qmd) covers regenerating R references.

CI runs the checks on macOS and Ubuntu, with fail-fast disabled so one platform's
failure does not cancel the other's. The packaging workflow tests Linux x86_64
and aarch64 at PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5.
